chunks: He said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is not a wrongdoer to His servants, nor a denier of blessings, nor heedless of what they do, nor unjust to the pious, nor unjust to the doers of good, nor unjust to the sincere.

key_terms.جَاحِدٍ: Denier / One who refuses to acknowledge

ai.seo_question: What are the key attributes of God regarding justice and blessings in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq uses this narration to reinforce the doctrine of divine justice (*Adl*), a cornerstone of Shia theology, by illustrating how God’s inherent fairness ensures that no deed, however small, is overlooked. This highlights the reciprocal nature of divine grace, where gratitude (*Shukr*) from the believer is met with proportional reward, affirming that God’s attention to the pious is both precise and unwavering.
